skill.name: testing
skill.description: Guides pytest test generation, review, coverage checks, and common test execution workflows.
skill.summary: Helps teams create, review, and run pytest tests with coverage and quality patterns.

content.value_statement: Teams often miss edge cases, coverage gaps, and test organization issues in Python projects. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused pytest workflow for planning, reviewing, and running tests.
actual_capabilities: Defines activation keywords for pytest, unittest, coverage, integration, e2e, performance, and security testing.
Lists commands for running pytest suites, marker filters, coverage reports, mutation testing, and Hypothesis statistics.
Sets coverage expectations, including 80% minimum coverage and branch coverage.
Recommends a tests directory layout for unit, integration, e2e, security, and performance tests.
Shows basic Arrange-Act-Assert and pytest fixture examples.
limitations: It is centered on pytest projects and may need adaptation for other test frameworks.
Only SKILL.md is included, so referenced workflow and context files are not available in this package.
It lists example commands but does not verify project dependencies or test configuration.
It needs source code context to propose project-specific assertions.

use_cases.title: Add Missing Unit Coverage
use_cases.description: Identify edge cases, fixtures, and assertion targets for Python functions that need stronger pytest coverage.

use_cases.title: Review Test Quality
use_cases.description: Evaluate existing tests for weak assertions, unclear organization, slow markers, and coverage gaps before release.

use_cases.title: Standardize Test Workflows
use_cases.description: Create a shared pytest structure with marker groups, coverage expectations, and repeatable local commands.

prompt_templates.title: Create Unit Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for focused test ideas.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing skill to identify unit test cases for this Python function. Include pytest naming, fixtures needed, and edge cases to cover.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my pytest suite for coverage gaps, weak assertions, slow tests, and fixture misuse. Return prioritized recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Integration Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an integration test plan for this feature. Separate unit, integration, and e2e responsibilities, then list data setup and failure cases.

prompt_templates.title: Build Full Test Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a complete testing workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a staged pytest strategy for unit, integration, e2e, security, and performance testing. Include markers, coverage goals, and commands to run each stage.

output_examples.input: Review a pytest suite before a release.
output: A prioritized list of missing edge cases and weak assertions.
Fixture cleanup suggestions for repeated setup data.
Coverage report guidance tied to unit and integration boundaries.

output_examples.input: Create a test plan for new API endpoints.
output: Unit test scenarios for validation and serialization behavior.
Integration cases for authentication, persistence, and error paths.
Marker guidance for separating fast tests from slower workflows.

output_examples.input: Prepare local testing steps for a Python project.
output_examples.output: A clear run sequence covering the full suite, marker-specific runs, coverage reporting, mutation testing, and property-based statistics.

best_practices: Confirm dependencies before running coverage, mutation, or property-based tests.
Separate fast unit tests from integration, e2e, security, and performance suites with markers.
Ask for assertions, edge cases, and fixtures, not only happy-path tests.
anti_patterns: Do not run project commands before reviewing expected side effects.
Do not treat an 80% coverage target as proof that behavior is fully tested.
Do not reuse generic pytest examples when project fixtures and naming differ.

faq.question: Is this skill only for pytest?
faq.answer: It is designed for pytest-based Python projects. Some planning ideas can be adapted to other test frameworks.

faq.question: Can it run tests for me?
faq.answer: It provides local command patterns. Actual execution depends on the connected tool, environment access, and user approval.

faq.question: Does the package include workflow files?
faq.answer: This package includes SKILL.md. Files referenced inside that document are not present in the scanned package.

faq.question: What coverage standard does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends a minimum of 80% coverage, branch coverage, and both HTML and terminal coverage reports.

faq.question: Does it support security and performance testing?
faq.answer: It includes those areas in its activation keywords and suggested test directory structure.

faq.question: Is the skill safe to inspect?
faq.answer: The available file contains documentation and local pytest command examples. Review project code before running any tests.
